Name: Cecilia Zemlak 
 Sex: Female  
Year of Birth: 1967  
Age: 58  
Medical Record Number (MRN): Not Specified 
Primary Care Context: Outpatient and episodic emergency department encounters Source 
Documentation: Longitudinal patient summary and encounter records 
Cecilia Zemlak is a middle-aged female with a documented history of multiple pregnancies, 
musculoskeletal injuries, respiratory infections, and later breast cancer, managed primarily in 
outpatient settings with intermittent utilization of acute care services.  
Her clinical history reflects a chronic but non-progressive disease profile, characterized by 
recurrent acute issues without evidence of advanced systemic disease or major complications 
beyond her cancer diagnosis.

Over multiple years of documented care, starting from birth in 1967, the patient demonstrates a 
trajectory of normal childhood development transitioning to episodic acute conditions in 
adulthood, including infections, injuries, and pregnancies. Healthcare utilization is consistent 
with routine well-child visits early on, evolving to management of acute bronchitis, sinusitis, 
sprains, fractures, and pregnancy-related events. A significant event is the diagnosis of stage 2 
breast cancer in 2020, with subsequent treatment. 
There is no evidence of prolonged hospitalization, intensive care utilization, or major 
cardiovascular events. The overall clinical course suggests moderate symptom burden with 
preserved functional status, allowing for ongoing ambulatory management. Social history 
consistently notes active smoking and alcoholism, which may contribute to health risks.

Malignant Neoplasm of Breast (Chronic, Confirmed) 
The patient carries a confirmed diagnosis of malignant neoplasm of breast (SNOMED CT 
254837009), staged as 2 with positive HER2, ER, and PR status.  
Diagnosed in 2020, it involved tumor size documentation and lymph node involvement.

• Surgical intervention (excision, biopsy) 
• No documented recurrence or metastasis in follow-up 
• Ongoing surveillance implied 
The cancer appears managed without current active complications. 
Essential Hypertension (Chronic, Confirmed) 
Intermittent blood pressure elevations are noted, but no explicit diagnosis is documented in 
excerpts. Vital signs show variable readings, occasionally elevated, without treatment initiation 
in early records. 
Chronic Intractable Migraine Without Aura (Episodic, Confirmed) 
Recurrent headaches with sinus pain, nasal congestion, sore throat, facial swelling, 
photophobia, and cough, consistent with migraine or sinus-related symptoms.

• Recurrent episodes 
• Associated symptoms 
• Partial response to treatments 
• No progressive neurologic disease

The record includes multiple pregnancies (normal and complicated by preeclampsia, tubal 
pregnancy, miscarriage), musculoskeletal injuries (sprains, fractures of ankle, wrist, clavicle), 
respiratory infections (acute bronchitis, viral pharyngitis, sinusitis), and childhood normal 
development.  
Breast cancer in 2020 is the major adult event, with no chronic sequelae from early issues 
documented.

Cecilia Zemlak is a 58-year-old female with a history of stage 2 breast cancer managed surgically, 
alongside episodic respiratory infections and musculoskeletal injuries, without evidence of 
chronic progressive disease or complications. Her history reflects multiple pregnancies and low 
healthcare needs beyond acute events.
